rites.name: Syuzis
rites.text: Syuzis is a concept of Tosistium, an idea of the Courts that binds oaths to the growing of grove-trees during the Age of the first sovereign. It is less a being than a principle that the courts invoke when a bargain must hold between kingdoms. Its power is measured in small, careful acts rather than destruction.

rites.name: Craston
rites.text: Craston is a concept of Tosistium's Holy Age, born in the years after the Fall, when the Sundering broke worlds into Shards and the Pact was sworn over the ruins. It is remembered as a discipline of flame and temple-keeping, the quiet craft by which the orders held their vows against the drift of the broken lands.

rites.name: Theishis
rites.text: Theishis is a concept of Tosistium, the act of breaking a bond between two things that had been joined. During the Age of Sundering it was the force that split old landholdings from their keepers when the Pact was sworn.

rites.name: Pelurar
rites.text: Pelurar is a concept in Tosistium, the idea that a broken bond can be mended by a single spoken word of the Pact. It was born in the Fall, when worlds split and the Sundering scattered their people across the Shards. Its power is measured in the small, binding gestures of oaths rather than in ruin.

rites.name: Grimokturn
rites.text: Grimokturn is a concept in Tosistium, born in the Walled Age when orders and churches held the land behind stone barriers. It names the first crossings made over those walls during the Holy Age of flame and temples. Its power rests on the idea that a threshold once crossed can never be fully closed again.

rites.name: Zephezith
rites.text: Zephezith is a concept of the Walled Age in Tosistium, a time of holding walls, sworn orders, and early churches that kept fragile settlements alive. Its meaning shifted during the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds and turned the wall-keepers into first crossers of open water.

rites.name: Vistium
rites.text: Vistium is a discipline of kinetic reflex practiced by the Tosh wayfarers, who train their bodies to store and release motion through taut, layered sinews. Its masters can briefly redirect a falling tree's momentum with a single open palm, though overuse leaves their joints brittle for weeks.

rites.name: Kelarde
rites.text: Kelarde is the idea that a single question can split the future into three paths, each one recorded on the shelves of the Library. In the Three Futures it is the shared name for the moment the ending branches, when the choice between them is still unmade.
